messages:
alex_sales: Hey team — we're winding down the AcmeCorp POC. Need a clear deprovision playbook so we can hand off to ops/security. Items we must cover: hosted API key rotation/revocation, drain + delete Dedicated pool `acme-poc`, VPC peering removal for Private, customer telemetry export, and confirmation of data retention after deletion. Who owns what and when?

maya_infra: I can take the dedicated pool work. Typical steps: scale pool to 0 to let in-flight requests finish, verify no active sessions in the allocator, then delete. Command we use in infra runbook: 
```
redwoodctl pools drain --name acme-poc --timeout 30m && redwoodctl pools delete acme-poc
```
I'll open an internal ticket with ETA. Prefer Fri morning to avoid business traffic.

sam_security: I'll own hosted API key rotation and final revoke. Safe sequence: create replacement key, update any customer-side config, then revoke the old key. For Private deployments we also need to rotate KMS key references if they used customer-managed keys. Also need written approval before deleting logs tied to PII.

jess_cs: Customer gave tentative OK for an export of telemetry to their S3. They asked for a 7-day post-POC retention of the export, but they're fine with us deleting our copies after export completes. I'll coordinate export and post the S3 presigned link here when ready.

alex_sales: Thanks. Quick Qs: 1) Does security need the API key ID to revoke? 2) Any compliance ticket required to delete logs or pool artifacts? 3) Who should notify the customer right before we run deletion?

maya_infra: 2) No compliance ticket for this class of POC teardown (internal policy), but we keep an audit entry in the infra ticket. 3) Ops announcement can come from the AE (alex_sales) — short window notice (30m) is fine.

sam_security: 1) Yes, I need the API key ID (or the key fingerprint). If the key is already rotated in customer side, we still need the old key ID to ensure full revocation. Also request that Jess confirm the export contains no unredacted PII. If PII: we follow the data handling checklist and need explicit opt-in to retain.

jess_cs: Copy — I'll validate the export and check for PII. I should have the export ready Thu 15:00 PT. Old key id (sent DM): ak_78x9b2f.

deprovision-bot: NOTE: Scheduled pool drain request received from maya_infra for `acme-poc` at 2026-04-10T17:00:00Z. This is a stub notification; confirm to schedule.

alex_sales: Proposed timeline (please ack):
- Thu 15:00 PT: telemetry export to customer S3 (jess_cs)
- Thu 16:00 PT: security creates rotation key and prepares revoke plan (sam_security)
- Fri 10:00 PT: drain and delete Dedicated pool `acme-poc` (maya_infra)
- Fri 10:30 PT: revoke old hosted API key `ak_78x9b2f` (sam_security)
- Fri 11:00 PT: remove VPC peering (if Private was used) and finalize artifacts (maya_infra)
Please react with :thumbsup: or call out blockers.

maya_infra: :thumbsup: I'll open the infra ticket now and put the schedule in the ticket.

sam_security: :thumbsup: I'll create the new key and DM the rotation steps to Alex and Jess before revoke.

jess_cs: :thumbsup: Export to S3 scheduled Thu 15:00 PT, will confirm link and PII check.

alex_sales: Great — I'll message the customer with the timeline and ask them to expect the S3 link. If anything changes, post updates here.

sam_security: One more note — after revoke we also rotate any internal service credentials that referenced the POC key (CI secrets, monitoring hooks). Maya, can you scan for references in infra?

maya_infra: Yep — will run a quick grep across infra repos and CI secrets manager and report false positives in the ticket.

alex_sales: Perfect. Thanks everyone — I'll close the loop with AcmeCorp once we have the export link and the infra ticket number.
